name: OpenAIRE_search_publications
description: Search OpenAIRE publications, datasets, or software with recoverable one-based pagination. Page size is 1-1000 and page * max_results must be <=10000. total_results is exact; accessible_results and upstream_truncated disclose the API's 10,000-result window.

query.description: Search query for OpenAIRE research products. Use keywords to search across titles, abstracts, and metadata.

max_results.description: Results per page (1-1000). Out-of-range values are rejected rather than silently clamped.

page.description: One-based page. OpenAIRE requires page * max_results <= 10000; continue with next_page while has_more is true.

type.description: Type of research product to search: 'publications', 'datasets', or 'software'. Default is 'publications'.

accessible_results.description: How many of the matches OpenAIRE will let a caller page through: min(total_results, 10000). Measured 10000 for 'machine learning'. THIS, NOT total_results, is the size of the set that can actually be retrieved.

has_more.description: True when another page exists WITHIN THE ACCESSIBLE WINDOW. It goes false at the 10,000-record ceiling even when more matches exist, so false does not mean the result set was exhausted -- `upstream_truncated` is what says that.

next_page.description: The page number to ask for next, or NULL when has_more is false. Null here plus upstream_truncated true means the rest of the matches cannot be reached at all.

page.description: Which page this is, as OpenAIRE's own response header reports it -- not necessarily the page asked for.

page_size.description: How many records a page holds, again as the header reports it. It can differ from the max_results asked for, so paging arithmetic must use THIS number.

returned.description: How many records are in `results` on this page. Measured 2 against total_results in the tens of thousands.

total_results_is_exact.description: Whether total_results is an exact count. IT IS HARD-CODED TRUE by this wrapper and has never been anything else, so it carries no information about the reply it appears in; it is declared here because a flag that cannot be false is worse than no flag when it is read as one that can.

upstream_truncated.description: True when total_results exceeds accessible_results -- more matches exist than the API will ever serve for this query. Measured TRUE for 'machine learning'. A count taken from total_results and a set built by paging will then disagree, and no amount of paging closes the gap; narrow the query instead.

warning.description: Present ONLY when OpenAIRE reports more than 10,000 matches: the human-readable form of upstream_truncated, saying that the API serves only the first 10,000 results for a query. It did not appear in every measured call, because whether it appears depends on the query's match count and not on the request.

name: OpenAIRE_search_projects
description: Search OpenAIRE funded projects/grants with recoverable one-based pagination. Page size is 1-1000, page * max_results must be <=10000, and metadata distinguishes exact total_results from the first 10,000 accessible matches. Returns grant code, title, funder, funding stream, dates, amounts, currency, and website.

query.description: Keyword(s) to search project titles, acronyms, and metadata (e.g., 'cancer', 'machine learning', 'graphene').

max_results.description: Projects per page (1-1000). OpenAIRE exposes at most the first 10,000 matches.

page.description: One-based page. page * max_results must not exceed 10000.

source.description: Which aggregator the row came from, e.g. 'OpenAIRE'.

type.description: The kind of OpenAIRE entity the row is, e.g. 'projects'. Constant for this tool; it exists because the same row shape is used for publications and datasets.

accessible_results.description: How many of the matches OpenAIRE will actually serve, e.g. 10000 -- against total_results of 338854 on the measured query. OpenAIRE's API caps deep paging, so this, not total_results, is the number of projects that can be retrieved.

has_more.description: True when a further page exists, e.g. true.

next_page.description: The page number to request next, e.g. 2. Null when there is none.

page.description: Which page this reply is, 1-based, e.g. 1.

page_size.description: How many results per page were requested, e.g. 1.

total_results_is_exact.description: True when total_results is an exact count rather than a lower bound, e.g. true.

upstream_truncated.description: True when OpenAIRE itself cut the result set, e.g. true. Set when total_results exceeds accessible_results.

warning.description: The limit OpenAIRE discloses about the query. Measured value: 'OpenAIRE reports more than 10,000 matches, but its API only allows the first 10,000 results for a query.' Any count derived by paging this search is bounded by that cap, not by the real total.

error.description: Short description of what went wrong, e.g. 'Network/API error calling OpenAIRE'. Present only on this branch; the success branch has no `error` key at all.

reason.description: The underlying exception text behind `error`, e.g. "HTTPSConnectionPool(host='api.openaire.eu', port=443): Read timed out. (read timeout=20)". This is what distinguishes a transient timeout, which is worth retrying, from a rejected query, which is not.
